In the densely wooded precinct rises a giant {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=camphor tree}} designated a national {{ill|Natural monument|ar|نصب تذكاري طبيعي|ast|Monumentu natural|ba|Тәбиғәт ҡомартҡыһы|be|Помнікі прыроды|be_x_old|Помнік прыроды|bg|Природна забележителност|bs|Spomenik prirode|ca|Monument natural|cs|Přírodní památka|da|Naturmonument|de|Naturdenkmal|eo|Naturmemorindaĵo|es|Monumento natural|et|Loodusmälestis|eu|Monumentu natural|fa|یادمان طبیعی|fi|Luonnonmuistomerkki|fr|Monument naturel|gl|Monumento natural|hr|Spomenik prirode|hy|Բնության հուշարձան|id|Monumen alam|is|Náttúruvætti|it|Monumento naturale|ja|天然記念物|ka|ბუნების ძეგლი|kk|Табиғат ескерткіші|ko|천연기념물|lv|Dabas piemineklis|mk|Споменик на природата|nl|Natuurmonument|nn|Naturminne|no|Naturminne|pl|Pomnik przyrody|pt|Monumento natural|ro|Monument al naturii|ru|Памятник природы|sh|Spomenik prirode|sk|Prírodná pamiatka|sl|Naravni spomenik|sq|Monument natyror|sr|Споменик природе|sv|Naturminne|th|อนุสรณ์สถานทางธรรมชาติ|tr|Tabiat anıtı|uk|Пам'ятка природи|uz|Tabiat yodgorliklari|zh|自然紀念物|qid=Q23790}}.

=== Shrine name ===
A {{ill|Munafuda|ja|棟札|zh|上樑記牌|qid=Q8008834}} of the present honden shows that in {{ill|Genroku|ar|فترة غنروكو|cs|Genroku|de|Genroku|es|Genroku|fa|گنروکو|fr|Ère Genroku|id|Genroku|it|Genroku|ja|元禄|ko|겐로쿠|pt|Genroku|ru|Гэнроку|simple|Genroku|sk|Genroku|sr|Генроку|sv|Genroku|tr|Genroku|zh|元祿|qid=Q1325001}} 10 ({{ill|1697|ab|1697|af|1697|als|1697|am|1697 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1697|ar|1697|ary|1697|arz|1697|ast|1697|avk|1697|az|1697|azb|۱۶۹۷ (میلادی)|ban|1697|bcl|1697|be|1697|be_x_old|1697|bg|1697|bn|১৬৯৭|bpy|মারি ১৬৯৭|br|1697|bs|1697.|ca|1697|cdo|1697 nièng|ceb|1697|ckb|١٦٩٧|crh|1697|cs|1697|csb|1697|cv|1697|cy|1697|da|1697|de|1697|diq|1697|el|1697|eml|1697|eo|1697|es|1697|et|1697|eu|1697|fa|۱۶۹۷ (میلادی)|fi|1697|fo|1697|fr|1697|frp|1697|frr|1697|fur|1697|fy|1697|ga|1697|gan|1697年|gcr|1697|gd|1697|gl|1697|gv|1697|he|1697|hi|१६९७|hr|1697.|hsb|1697|ht|1697 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1697|hy|1697|hyw|1697 թուական|ia|1697|id|1697|ilo|1697|io|1697|is|1697|it|1697|ja|1697年|jv|1697|ka|1697|kaa|1697|kk|1697 жыл|ko|1697년|krc|1697 джыл|la|1697|lb|1697|lij|1697|lmo|1697|lt|1697 m.|lv|1697. gads|mai|१६९७|map_bms|1697|mdf|1697|mg|1697|mhr|1697|mi|1697|min|1697|mk|1697|mr|इ.स. १६९७|mrj|1697 и|ms|1697|my|၁၆၉၇|myv|1697 ие|mzn|۱۶۹۷|nah|1697|nap|1697|nds|1697|new|सन् १६९७|nl|1697|nn|1697|no|1697|nrm|1697|nso|1697|oc|1697|olo|1697|or|୧୬୯୭|os|1697-æм аз|pl|1697|pnb|1697|pt|1697|qu|1697|ro|1697|ru|1697 год|rue|1697|sa|१६९७|sah|1697|scn|1697|sd|1697ع|se|1697|sh|1697.|shn|1697|simple|1697|sk|1697|sl|1697|smn|1697|sq|1697|sr|1697|su|1697|sv|1697|sw|1697|szl|1697|ta|1697|te|1697|tg|Соли 1697|th|พ.ศ. 2240|tk|1697|tl|1697|tly|1697|tr|1697|tt|1697 ел|uk|1697|ur|1697ء|uz|1697|vec|1697|vi|1697|vls|1697|wa|1697|war|1697|wuu|1697年|xmf|1697|yi|1697|zh|1697年|zh_min_nan|1697 nî|zh_yue|1697年|qid=Q7702}}) it was called "Kuzumi Taisha." Earlier names include "Kusumi Shrine" and "Kugo Taisha," and after the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}} it was renamed to the current form<ref name="神社志">'Shizuoka-ken Jinja-shi,' Shizuoka-ken Chōdo Kenkyūkai, 1941.</ref>. In this case, the shrine name is derived from local place names (ancient {{ill|Itō, Shizuoka|ar|إتو (شيزوكا)|arz|اتو (تجمع سكان فى محافظه شيزوكا)|azb|ایتو، شیزوئوکا|ce|Ито (гӀала)|ceb|Itō|da|Itō (Shizuoka)|de|Itō (Shizuoka)|eo|Ito (Ŝizuoka)|es|Itō (Shizuoka)|et|Itō|fa|ایتو، شیزوئوکا|fi|Itō (Shizuoka)|fr|Itō|gl|Itō|he|איטו (יפן)|hu|Itó (Sizuoka)|id|Itō, Shizuoka|it|Itō|ja|伊東市|ko|이토시|lt|Itas|mzn|ایتو، شیزوئوکا|nl|Ito (Shizuoka)|pl|Itō|pt|Ito (Shizuoka)|ro|Itō (localitate)|ru|Ито (город)|sv|Ito|tg|Ито|th|อิโต|tl|Itō|tr|Itō|tt|Ито (шәһәр)|uk|Іто (Сідзуока)|ur|ایٹو، شیزوکا|vi|Itō, Shizuoka|war|Itō, Shizuoka|zh|伊東市|zh_classical|伊東市|zh_min_nan|Itô-chhī|zh_yue|伊東|qid=Q721163|lt=Kusumi-gō}}, medieval Kusumi / Kuzumi / Nanmi-shō). It is thought the old reading "kutsumi" voiced to "kuzumi" and became current "kuzumi"<ref name="調査報告">'Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku.'</ref>. The site belonged to Oka village until early modern times, and up to {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 47 ({{ill|1972|ab|1972|af|1972|als|1972|am|1972 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1972|ar|1972|ary|1972|arz|1972|ast|1972|av|1972 сон|avk|1972|az|1972|azb|۱۹۷۲ (میلادی)|ba|1972 йыл|ban|1972|bar|1972|bat_smg|1972|bcl|1972|be|1972|be_x_old|1972|bg|1972|bh|1972|bjn|1972|bn|১৯৭২|bpy|মারি ১৯৭২|br|1972|bs|1972.|btm|1972|ca|1972|cbk_zam|1972|cdo|1972 nièng|ce|1972 шо|ceb|1972|ckb|١٩٧٢|co|1972|crh|1972|cs|1972|csb|1972|cv|1972|cy|1972|da|1972|de|1972|diq|1972|dsb|1972|el|1972|eml|1972|eo|1972|es|1972|et|1972|eu|1972|fa|۱۹۷۲|fi|1972|fiu_vro|1972|fo|1972|fr|1972|frp|1972|frr|1972|fur|1972|fy|1972|ga|1972|gag|1972|gan|1972年|gcr|1972|gd|1972|gl|1972|gn|1972|gv|1972|hak|1972-ngièn|he|1972|hi|१९७२|hif|1972|hr|1972.|hsb|1972|ht|1972 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1972|hy|1972|hyw|1972 թուական|ia|1972|id|1972|ilo|1972|inh|1972 шу|io|1972|is|1972|it|1972|ja|1972年|jbo|1972moi|jv|1972|ka|1972|kaa|1972|kbp|1972|kk|1972 жыл|kn|೧೯೭೨|ko|1972년|krc|1972 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1972|ku|1972|kv|1972-ӧд во|kw|1972|la|1972|lb|1972|lez|1972 йис|li|1972|lij|1972|lmo|1972|ln|1972|lt|1972 m.|lv|1972. gads|mai|१९७२|map_bms|1972|mdf|1972|mg|1972|mhr|1972|mi|1972|min|1972|mk|1972|ml|1972|mn|1972 он|mr|इ.स. १९७२|mrj|1972 и|ms|1972|my|၁၉၇၂|myv|1972 ие|mzn|۱۹۷۲|nah|1972|nap|1972|nds|1972|nds_nl|1972|nl|1972|nn|1972|no|1972|nrm|1972|nso|1972|oc|1972|olo|1972|or|୧୯୭୨|os|1972-æм аз|pa|1972|pam|1972|pap|1972|pl|1972|pnb|1972|pt|1972|qu|1972|ro|1972|roa_tara|1972|ru|1972 год|rue|1972|sah|1972|sc|1972|scn|1972|sd|1972ع|se|1972|sh|1972.|shn|1972|si|1972|simple|1972|sk|1972|sl|1972|smn|1972|so|1972|sq|1972|sr|1972|stq|1972|su|1972|sv|1972|sw|1972|szl|1972|ta|1972|te|1972|tg|Соли 1972|th|พ.ศ. 2515|tk|1972|tl|1972|tly|1972|tpi|1972|tr|1972|tt|1972 ел|ty|1972|udm|1972 ар|ug|1972 - يىلى|uk|1972|ur|1972ء|uz|1972|vec|1972|vi|1972|vls|1972|vo|1972|wa|1972|war|1972|wuu|1972年|xmf|1972|yi|1972|za|1972 nienz|zea|1972|zh|1972年|zh_classical|一九七二年|zh_min_nan|1972 nî|zh_yue|1972年|qid=Q2476}}) the address was Ito-shi Oka Aza Miyanoue, so it is still commonly called "Oka no Gōsha."

=== Enshrined deities ===
The principal deity is '''Kuzumi deity''', with {{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto}} ({{ill|Inari Ōkami|abstract|Q719665|ar|إناري|az|İnari Okami|ban|Inari (Kami)|bcl|Inari Ōkami|ca|Oinari|cs|Inari (mytologie)|da|Inari|de|Inari (Kami)|el|Ινάρι Όκαμι|es|Inari (Japón)|et|Inari (jumal)|eu|Inari Ōkami|fa|ایناری|fi|Inari (kami)|fr|Inari (divinité japonaise)|hr|Inari|hu|Inari (sintó)|hy|Ինարի Օկամի|id|Inari (Kami)|it|Inari (mitologia)|ja|稲荷神|jv|Inari (Kami)|ko|이나리노카미|mni|ꯏꯅꯔꯤ ꯑꯣꯀꯃꯤ|ne|इनारी ओकामी|nl|Inari Ōkami|no|Inari|pl|Inari (bóstwo)|pt|Inari Ōkami|ru|Инари (божество)|simple|Inari Ōkami|sl|Inari (mitologija)|sr|Инари (богиња)|sv|Inari|tok|jan sewi suli Inali|tr|Inari Ōkami|uk|Інарі (міфологія)|vi|Inari Ōkami|zh|稻荷神|qid=Q719665}}) in the {{ill|Aidono|ja|相殿|qid=Q135009883}}.

The principal deity is variously said to be {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611}} or a related clan deity, or medicinal deities such as {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q276944}} and {{ill|Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|qid=Q3275687}}, but none is certain. Since sites in this area date back to the {{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}}, it is considered to have been inhabited early and the deity likely revered from old times as the tutelary deity of the area<ref name="調査報告"/>. The aiden deity was invited later by the {{ill|Itō clan|Q2975280|qid=Q2975280}}; because their ancestor {{ill|Kudō Suketaka|Q24860857|qid=Q24860857|lt=Kudō Suketaka (Kudō Ietsugu / Itō Ietsugu)}} revered Inari, it is thought Inari was merged here<ref name="調査報告"/><ref name="神々">'Nihon no Kamigami.'</ref>. The Itō lineage is said to have followed Suketaka in revering Inari, and among branches dispersed to various regions there were many cases of inviting Inari at their new settlements<ref name="神々"/>.

=== Origin and history ===
From ancient times, rites were likely performed to the sacred grove where divine spirit dwelled, still flourishing in the precinct today<ref name="調査報告"/>. The "Kuzumi Shrine" in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}' is considered this shrine<ref>There is also a theory identifying it with {{ill|Yuzen Shrine|Q11563474|qid=Q11563474}} in {{ill|Atami|Q653364|qid=Q653364}} (e.g., 'Nihon Chiri Shiryō').</ref>, but its name does not appear in the '{{ill|Izu no Kuni Shinkaichō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}},' a {{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|Q11420490|qid=Q11420490}}.

In the medieval period it received reverence and protection from the Itō clan based in this area. Itō Suketaka repaired the shrine and founded nearby Tōrin-ji as a {{ill|Bettō-ji|ja|別当寺|qid=Q11396755}} to manage it<ref>'Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku.' Tōrin-ji's mountain name is "Inari-zan," thought to derive from enshrining Inari ('Nihon no Kamigami'). There is also a tradition that it was founded by Sukechika (Suketaka's grandson) to pray for the soul of his son {{ill|Kawazu Sukeyasu|Q11553998|qid=Q11553998|lt=Sukeyasu}}, slain by {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|Q11479615|qid=Q11479615}}, his in-law cousin (same source). See also "{{ill|Revenge of the Soga Brothers|Q10324810|qid=Q10324810}}."</ref>. Though Itō power declined after death of Suketaka's grandson {{ill|Itō Sukechika|Q11379553|qid=Q11379553|lt=Sukechika}}, descendants remaining nearby appear to have continued faith in the shrine<ref name="調査報告"/>. According to shrine munafuda, in {{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 15 ({{ill|1610|Q6765|qid=Q6765}}), {{ill|Itō Masayo|Q9385264|qid=Q9385264|lt=Itō Masa(yo)yo}} rebuilt after fire (though this is said to refer to the stone hokora for Inari/Hōsō deity under the great camphor noted below<ref>Akiyama Akira, 'Tōshū Shikō,' written in {{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} 12 (1800).</ref>). Until {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, local rulers periodically donated rice offerings<ref name="神社志"/>.

In Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|ab|1873|af|1873|als|1873|am|1873 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1873|ar|1873|ary|1873|arz|1873|ast|1873|avk|1873|az|1873|azb|۱۸۷۳ (میلادی)|ba|1873 йыл|ban|1873|bar|1873|bat_smg|1873|bcl|1873|be|1873|be_x_old|1873|bg|1873|bn|১৮৭৩|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৩|br|1873|bs|1873.|ca|1873|cdo|1873 nièng|ce|1873 шо|ceb|1873|ckb|١٨٧٣|crh|1873|cs|1873|csb|1873|cv|1873|cy|1873|da|1873|de|1873|diq|1873|el|1873|eml|1873|eo|1873|es|1873|et|1873|eu|1873|fa|۱۸۷۳|fi|1873|fiu_vro|1873|fo|1873|fr|1873|frp|1873|frr|1873|fur|1873|fy|1873|ga|1873|gan|1873年|gcr|1873|gd|1873|gl|1873|gv|1873|he|1873|hi|१८७३|hif|1873|hr|1873.|hsb|1873|ht|1873 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1873|hy|1873|hyw|1873 թուական|ia|1873|id|1873|ilo|1873|inh|1873 шу|io|1873|is|1873|it|1873|ja|1873年|jv|1873|ka|1873|kaa|1873|kk|1873 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೩|ko|1873년|krc|1873 джыл|ku|1873|kv|1873-ӧд во|la|1873|lb|1873|lez|1873 йис|li|1873|lij|1873|lmo|1873|lt|1873 m.|lv|1873. gads|mai|१८७३|map_bms|1873|mdf|1873|mg|1873|mhr|1873|mi|1873|min|1873|mk|1873|ml|1873|mr|इ.स. १८७३|mrj|1873 и|ms|1873|my|၁၈၇၃|myv|1873 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۳|nah|1873|nap|1873|nds|1873|nds_nl|1873|new|ई सं १८७३|nl|1873|nn|1873|no|1873|nrm|1873|nso|1873|oc|1873|olo|1873|or|୧୮୭୩|os|1873-æм аз|pa|1873|pl|1873|pnb|1873|pt|1873|qu|1873|ro|1873|ru|1873 год|rue|1873|sa|१८७३|sah|1873 сыл|sc|1873|scn|1873|sd|1873ع|se|1873|sh|1873.|shn|1873|si|1873|simple|1873|sk|1873|sl|1873|smn|1873|sq|1873|sr|1873|stq|1873|su|1873|sv|1873|sw|1873|szl|1873|ta|1873|te|1873|tg|Соли 1873|th|พ.ศ. 2416|tk|1873|tl|1873|tly|1873|tr|1873|tt|1873 ел|udm|1873 ар|ug|1873 - يىلى|uk|1873|ur|1873ء|uz|1873|vec|1873|vi|1873|vls|1873|vo|1873|wa|1873|war|1873|wuu|1873年|xmf|1873|yi|1873|za|1873 nienz|zea|1873|zh|1873年|zh_classical|一八七三年|zh_min_nan|1873 nî|zh_yue|1873年|qid=Q7757}}) April, it was ranked gōsha.

The shrine was also treated as sacred by nearby residents. It is said funeral processions were strictly forbidden from passing the road in front of the shrine; even though it was the main road to Tōrin-ji, funeral routes to that temple used detours<ref name="神々"/>.

=== Rituals ===
=== Shinto rites ===
Until early modern times, festival day was September 19; after calendar reform it changed to October 19, and now the annual festival is October 15. At the festival, "Oka Kagura," {{ill|Sanbasō|Q11356796|qid=Q11356796}}, and Torisashi dance are dedicated at the precinct chōya building. "Oka Kagura" was originally a {{ill|Lion dance|Q713866|qid=Q713866}} performed on the first horse day of February<ref>Tateo Hamano, 'Itō-shi,' written in {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125|lt=Kaei era}} (mid-19th century).</ref>, thought to be a rite related to Inari<ref name="神々"/>. After a period of interruption, it was revived in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 59 and has been dedicated at the annual festival. Torisashi dance is also dedicated at other city shrines; each takes motifs from '{{ill|Soga Monogatari|Q217886|qid=Q217886}}' and depicts the Soga brothers, disguised as bird catchers, avenging their father. Sanbasō is also widely distributed as ritual performance across the {{ill|Izu Peninsula|Q822822|qid=Q822822}}<ref name="神々"/>.

=== Priests ===
In early modern times, Tōrin-ji managed the shrine as bettō<ref>The temple was a Shugendō temple of the {{ill|Tōzan-ha|Q11487826|qid=Q11487826}} since the {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853}} era (first half of 16th c.); now {{ill|Sōtō|Q749085|qid=Q749085}} ('Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku').</ref>, but at the start of Meiji, with {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, its monk returned to lay status, took the surname Asahi, and the Asahi family has continued the office.

=== Shrine buildings ===
[[File:Kuzumi-jinja no Ōkusu 20100612.jpg|thumb|150px|Hōsō deity and giant camphor]]
The honden is a 2-ken-square {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|es|Shinmeizukuri|fr|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|ru|Симмэй-дзукури|tr|Shinmei-zukuri|zh|神明造|qid=Q930545}} structure protected by a covering building ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=ooiya}}), rebuilt in Genroku 10. Its transom has carvings of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=foxes}} and other motifs. The covering structure dates from the {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045|lt=Tenpō period}} (early 19th c.). The haiden is a steel-reinforced concrete {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} tiled building, 3 bays by 2 bays, built in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 40.

=== Precinct shrines ===
Kumano Shrine, Hakusan Shrine, Mishima Shrine, Hachiman Shrine (merging Shinmei and Kasuga shrines), and Hōsō deity shrine. Hōsō deity is enshrined in a stone hokora under the giant camphor natural monument; because some gazetteers call it "Inari," it is thought Inari was worshiped here as {{ill|Smallpox demon|Q7543689|qid=Q7543689}}<ref name="神々"/>.

=== Cultural property ===
*{{ill|Great Camphor of Kuzumi Shrine|Q11621016|qid=Q11621016}} - a giant camphor north (left) of the haiden, trunk circumference about 15 m at chest height. Said to be over 1,000 years old<ref>Also described as reaching 2,000 years as of {{ill|March 18|Q2422|qid=Q2422}} in 'Nihon no Kamigami'.</ref>; designated national natural monument on February 28, {{ill|1933|Q18726|qid=Q18726}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 8).
